_comment: Calibrated 2026-08-27 against the 591-image fixture set in images/ — see research/RESULTS.md, camera-thresholds. Read by BOTH the app camera gate and the server quality gate, at runtime, never bundled. Every number here is answerable: images/check.py measures the set, images/calibrate.py scores these numbers against it. Do not move one without a named fixture and a RESULTS.md row.
_blur: The capture gate measures a 240x180 downscale, which destroys the very defect it is looking for — it flags 23 of 166 known-blurred fixtures, against 152 at full resolution. So this number is an advisory on the phone; the hard reject lives in _enhance_only below.
_fill: fill_fraction_max is deliberately 1.0, i.e. off. The busy box spanning the frame is what a product photograph looks like — at 0.90 this refused 44 of 93 good fixtures as 'too close', including every patterned-background one. Nothing needs it: all 83 too-far fixtures sit at fill 0.11, far below fill_fraction_min.
_camera_only: Below here is the live capture gate only — the server has no preview frames to run these against.
_enhance_only: Server enhancement pipeline only — the app never reads these. Reconciliation §6.
_crop: crop_fill_target is the product's long side as a fraction of the square listing canvas, and it is the only knob — the reconciliation also proposed crop_padding_pct: 8, which is the same number said backwards ((1 - 0.85) / 2 = 7.5% margin per side). Two keys that can disagree about one measurement is a bug waiting to happen, so there is one. Not calibrated against fixtures: 0.85 is the marketplace requirement (spec §9.1), not a measurement of our photographs.
_tiers: Mask confidence and tiers A/B/C. Scored against seg-v1 on 2026-08-28 by research/segmentation/tiers.py: these values catch 5 of the 7 masks a person would refuse to ship, and demote 2 good masks to tier B, which is a safe outcome. A grid search over area/uncertainty/blob values found nothing that does better on this set, so these stay as the reconciliation proposed them — now measured rather than reasoned. What they do NOT catch is in RESULTS.md, and it is a real gap, not a rounding error.
_tone: Contrast and shadow work, product region only. CLAHE runs on the L channel of LAB and nowhere else — on RGB it shifts hue, and a saree changing shade is exactly the misrepresentation the colour lock exists to catch (spec §5.3). The black/white points are percentiles of the product's own lightness, so a dark product is not stretched to look like a bright one. NOT calibrated against fixtures: these are the spec's numbers, and the fixture set has no photograph taken in real artisan light to calibrate them on.
_tone_edge_blur: How far the tone correction fades out across the mask edge, in pixels at the 2000px master. The one tone number that IS measured: BiRefNet's alpha ramps over 3-4px, and on pottery-potter-indoor-04 an 11.1 L correction across that ramp is 3.3 L per pixel, which draws a visible line around the product on tier C. At 4 the ramp is ~11px and the same correction is ~1 L/px. Guarded by test_the_tone_edge_is_not_a_visible_seam, which needs the model and skips without it. Deliberately NOT pipeline.FEATHER_PX: that is tier B's edge treatment and answers a different question.
